inputSnapshot.learningGoal: TypeScript discriminated union과 runtime validation을 배우고 싶다

round.generationRationale: The candidates use typed variants at different boundaries and interactions.

diversityCheck.rationale: Replay, form simulation and contract change review have distinct users and data flows.

candidates.title: Webhook Replay Microscope
candidates.summary: Replay redacted webhook variants and inspect which typed branch handled each event.
candidates.coreInteraction: Paste a redacted payload, choose a provider profile and step through variant narrowing.
candidates.usageMoment: When an integration receives an unfamiliar or failing webhook.
candidates.appeal: Turns opaque payload debugging into a visible event timeline.
candidates.technologyNecessity: Every provider event requires runtime validation before a discriminated union can narrow it safely.

evaluation.rationale: Typed variants are the central debugger model.
No personal need was supplied, but the tool is reusable.
It runs locally with redacted samples.
Three provider variants are enough for a beginner MVP.
The MVP avoids live integrations.
Schema errors need clear presentation.
A local TypeScript web app is sufficient.
The step-through event model differs from forms and change review.

candidates.title: Form State Variant Lab
candidates.summary: Model a multi-step form as explicit states and simulate valid and invalid transitions.
candidates.coreInteraction: Move a form through editing, validating, submitting and rejected states on a state map.
candidates.usageMoment: Before implementing a form with several async outcomes.
candidates.appeal: Makes hidden UI state bugs tangible without writing a full product.
candidates.technologyNecessity: A discriminant prevents impossible combinations of loading, success and error fields.
risks: A large state graph can become noisy

evaluation.rationale: The product visualizes union states directly.
It supports future projects rather than a stated need.
No external users or approval are needed.
A fixed state set keeps the MVP approachable.
Simulation avoids backend work.
Diagram layout is delegated to Agent Support.
It can run as a static TypeScript app.
Interactive transitions differ from payload replay.

candidates.title: API Contract Change Radar
candidates.summary: Compare two response examples and classify compatible, added and breaking variants.
candidates.coreInteraction: Drop before-and-after JSON examples into a comparison board and review typed change cards.
candidates.usageMoment: Before updating a client against a changed API response.
candidates.appeal: Provides a concrete answer to what a payload change can break.
candidates.technologyNecessity: Runtime schemas establish the boundary and union variants classify change outcomes.
risks: Examples cannot prove every production payload

evaluation.rationale: Typed change categories are the core output.
The input gave an interest, not a direct need.
Redacted samples are enough to use it locally.
Compatibility rules need a narrow initial set.
The MVP compares samples only.
Deep JSON comparison needs careful limits.
It can run locally without accounts.
Before-and-after review is distinct from replay and simulation.
